chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man upon whom the Hajj of Islam was due, and who made a vow in gratitude that he would send a man with it to Mecca for Hajj. Then the one who made the vow died before performing the Hajj of Islam and before fulfilling the vow that he had vowed.

He عليه السلام said: "If he left wealth, the Hajj of Islam is to be performed on his behalf from all of the estate, and from one-third of it there should be taken what will send a man for Hajj on account of his vow, and thus the vow has been fulfilled. But if he did not leave wealth except only the amount by which the Hajj of Islam may be performed, then Hajj is to be performed on his behalf from what he left, and his heir should perform on his behalf the vowed Hajj; it is only like a debt upon him."

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory Hajj binding upon a Muslim
key_terms.دَيْنٍ: a debt, indicating a binding liability
key_terms.شُكْرٍ: gratitude, as the motive for making the vow
key_terms.نَذَرَ: he made a vow binding himself to an act

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a deceased person used when he owed both Hajjat al-Islam and a vowed Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a deceased person who owed both the obligatory Hajj of Islam and a vowed Hajj. The obligatory Hajj is taken from the full estate, while the vowed Hajj is fulfilled from one-third if possible; if the estate only covers the obligatory Hajj, the heir performs the vowed Hajj because the vow is treated like a debt.
